title: Home's MCP tools (contract 10)
description: The tools the hub-side MCP server `hub` gives Home's Claude Code session on the hub VM, beside web-chat's 24 against Home's own daemon. Each tool is a thin caller of the typed requests it names (10-hub-request.json) under the Home principal, the service user svc_home authenticating with its api_key (03 C-03.16); it holds no right the requests do not grant. Contract 10, C-10.23 to C-10.28.

server_name.description: The MCP server name Home's session registers.

name.description: The tool name; Claude Code shows it as mcp__hub__<name>.

description.description: The description Claude reads. Load-bearing: it is part of the contract (C-10.27).

inputSchema.description: The tool's inputSchema, written in web-chat's style (properties described, required named).

backing.description: The typed requests the tool makes (C-10.23).

needs.description: What the Home principal must hold, in 04's words.

workspace.description: A workspace name or id; only its chats.

project.description: A project name or id; only its chats.

include_archived.description: Include archived chats (they are read only). Default false.

since.description: Epoch ms; list only conversations active since then. Default: 24 hours back.

conversation_id.description: Which listed conversation's turns to return. Default: the most recently active one.

before.description: Page back: the `next_before` of your previous read of that conversation; turns before it. Default: the newest page.

include.description: Which parts to return. Default: all four.

since.description: The last seq you read on this stream.

epoch.description: The epoch that since belongs to, from the previous answer.

limit.description: At most this many entries, up to 500. Default 100.

text.description: The message, written as the user would write it to that chat. At most 3000 characters.

reason.description: One line for the user's Today board: why you sent it. At most 280 characters.

send.description: auto (default): when that Claude is free; now: at once; hold: queue it unsent for the user.

conversation_id.description: A conversation in that chat, if not its primary one.

dashboard_id.description: The dashboard (list it through the user's request or the Board).

chat_id.description: The chat whose pane to mirror.

mount_id.description: The pane's mount id on that chat's page.

title.description: A label for the mirror; default the pane's own.

place.description: Proposed placement on the dashboard's 12-column grid, as web-chat's render takes it: col (1 to 12), span (2 to 12), rows (2 to 24 rows of 40px). Omit for full width.

id.description: Stable pane id on the dashboard; reuse it to update in place. Prefix it (e.g. "home-releases").

html.description: The pane's HTML/JS, as web-chat's render takes it.

params.description: Injected into the pane script as `params`. `title` labels the pane header.

store.description: A patch merged into the dashboard's store before the render; the pane can read and subscribe to it.

after.description: Place the pane after this pane or markdown id, or "start".

place.description: Proposed placement on the dashboard's 12-column grid, as web-chat's render takes it: col (1 to 12), span (2 to 12), rows (2 to 24 rows of 40px). Omit for full width.

force.description: Take over a pane another writer owns. Only when the user asked.

mode.description: query: events by source, kind, person, subject and time, newest first; search: by meaning, with text; count: only how many match.

source.description: One EventsDB source the user enabled: signal, imessage, email, discord, onecal, health, cronometer, findmy, git, claude.

kinds.description: Only these event kinds, at most 8.

persons.description: Only events naming these EventsDB person ids, at most 8.

subject.description: Only this subject (a thread, a calendar, a session).

since.description: From this RFC 3339 instant, or a window back from now (PT6H, P1D).

text.description: search only: what to look for, at most 200 characters. Never recorded.

limit.description: At most this many events, up to 200. Default 50. Not for count.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of your previous answer, for the next page. Not for count.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled records (spent, switched off, or waiting for the user's confirm). Default false.

checkin_id.description: Edit this record (one you made, from list_check_ins). Omit to create.

label.description: Its name on the user's Scheduled list, at most 120 characters.

trigger.description: Exactly one trigger. {kind: "cron", expr: "0 9 * * 1-5", zone: "America/New_York"}; {kind: "interval", every_s: 3600} (at least 300); {kind: "one_shot", at: "2026-12-01T09:00:00-05:00"}; {kind: "events_count", query: {source, kinds?, persons?, subject?, since: a window such as "PT15M"}, every_s: 900} (polled, at least 300; needs a condition).

every_s.description: interval and events_count: seconds, at least 300.

query.description: events_count: the read_events filter fields, since as a window (PT15M, P1D).

condition.description: events_count only, and required there: {field: "count", op: one of eq ne gt ge lt le, value: an integer}. The hub checks it before anything reaches you.

instruction.description: What you will be asked to do when it fires, verbatim, at most 3000 characters.

destination.description: {kind: home_page | dashboard | push | silence}; dashboard_id with dashboard only.

autonomy.description: notify: report on your own surfaces; draft: anything you would send outward is held for the user.

zone.description: The user's IANA zone for the forecast. Default: the user's setting.

hub_msg_id.description: The id the check-in message names (hm_...).

outcome.description: done: you did it; nothing: nothing to report; failed: you could not; held: a message you delegated for it waits on the user.

fetch_id.description: Only to read a result the hub held for you: the fetch_id of an earlier pending answer, alone. Answered once; then not_found.

kind.description: url: a page, your terms as the path after an allowed prefix; search: the host's search, your terms as the query.

host.description: One host from home_status fetch.hosts that allows this kind. No scheme, no port, no path.

path.description: search: one of the host's prefixes exactly. url: one of them, then your terms in order, each percent-encoded, joined by /. Starts with /, no ? or #.

terms.description: 1 to 8 terms, each copied exactly from a message the user wrote to you in the last 7 days, at most 120 characters each. Each counts against today's budget.

purpose.description: Why, in your words, at most 280 characters: shown to the user on the card, never sent.
